The system scales or masks the asset, so its identifying center must remain clear at small sizes.

Why an App Icon needs its own adaptation

The system changes its frame and size: The Home Screen, search, and Settings may use different sizes or platform shapes. Keep the main artwork inside a safe area so masking does not remove text or key contours.

Simplification is more reliable than extra detail: An App Icon identifies the whole app, so a small display should preserve one clear core shape. Platform variants can adapt the artwork while remaining recognizable as the same app.

It is not a Logo, Favicon, or UI Icon

App Icon is the image used to identify an app in system surfaces; a Logo is a brand mark; a Favicon serves browser-site surfaces; an Icon communicates a UI function. They may share a source, but a horizontal Logo or toolbar icon cannot simply be shrunk and shipped as the App Icon.

You can say this to an AI Agent

“

Create a simplified square App Icon from the existing brand shape with a clear recognition center that survives system masking. Check scaling and cropping on the Home Screen, system search, and Settings. Do not change in-app action icons or treat a platform size list as the acceptance result.
